Article Title: PM Modi inaugurates global conference on environment, climate dynamics
Article Text:
The conference is being held on September 19 and 20

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated a two-day international conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”, organised by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi.The conference, being held on September 19 and 20, brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from India and abroad. Judicial representatives from 17 countries are also participating in the event.Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav, Attorney General R Venkataramani and NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava attended the inaugural session.The conference will feature four technical sessions focusing on key environmental and climate-related issues. According to the NGT, the discussions will examine major challenges facing the world, identify gaps in policy-making and implementation, and explore ways to strengthen institutional cooperation.The event also aims to facilitate the exchange of successful environmental practices and strengthen environmental justice amid growing challenges linked to climate change, development and governance.President Droupadi Murmu will attend the valedictory session on Sunday. Union minister Manohar Lal, Supreme Court judge Justice PS Narasimha, NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta are also scheduled to attend the concluding session.The conference is expected to work towards developing a roadmap for addressing present and future environmental and climate challenges.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated a two-day international conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ The conference, being held on September 19 and 20, brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from India and abroad.

Article Title: US national gets default bail in terror case
Article Text:
Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi has granted default bail to US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke

NEW DELHI: A special NIA court in Delhi Friday granted default bail to the US national arrested in March on terror charges for allegedly helping ethnic armed groups in India and Myanmar, days after the "incomplete" chargesheet filed by the investigating agency dropped charges under UAPA, reports Koushiki Saha.While granting bail to Matthew Aaron VanDyke, who has spent 180 days in custody, the court noted NIA's failure to complete its probe. It cannot be concluded that the accused is not entitled to default bail merely because an agency says a probe is far from over, the court said.VanDyke had sought default bail Thursday, contending that under Section 43D(2) proviso (1) of the anti-terror law, the investigation was required to be completed within 180 days, which ended on Sept 8.
Article Summary: US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke was arrested in March on terror charges for allegedly helping ethnic armed groups in India and Myanmar. A special NIA court in Delhi Friday granted default bail to the US national. The court noted NIA's failure to complete its probe. It cannot be concluded that the accused is not entitled to default bail merely because an agency says a probe is far from over.

Article Title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
Article Text:
A street vendor sells walnuts on the occasion of the Sayar festival, in Mandi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. “My back aches now,” Ahmad said. J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output.Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. “We have been doing it for centuries,” said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesn’t help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries. “There is no mechanism to address the issue,” Bhat said.Ahmad’s younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmir’s walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. “When someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,” Ashfaq A. Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUAST’s Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. “It is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,” Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. “They have higher productivity and better export potential. There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,” he said.The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.
Article Summary: J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees.

Article Title: 'Will take all necessary actions': India's stern warning amid reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 bilateral pacts
Article Text:
EA breaks silence on reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 pacts

NEW DELHI: India on Friday said it would take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests after reports that Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding signed with New Delhi during the previous Awami League government.Responding to news agency ANI, at the ministry of external affairs’ bi-weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said New Delhi had not received any formal communication from Dhaka on the review.“We also have seen some media reports on this matter, but nothing has been conveyed to us officially. Obviously, India will take all necessary actions to protect its interests,” Jaiswal said.Bangladesh’s ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has said the agreements are being examined with the country’s national interests in mind. chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni said last week, “We are reviewing the agreements that mean 101 MoUs and you will get its (review) result soon.”The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports, connectivity and other bilateral projects. Dhaka has not announced a blanket cancellation of the agreements.The developments come as India-Bangladesh ties face scrutiny over trade, transit, energy, border management and water-sharing issues. India has previously extended more than $7 billion through Lines of Credit for infrastructure projects in Bangladesh, while bilateral arrangements have also enabled the movement of Indian cargo through Bangladeshi ports.Water-sharing remains another key issue. The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is due to expire in December 2026, while the long-pending Teesta agreement remains unresolved.On Friday, Jaiswal said existing mechanisms for discussions on shared rivers remained operational.“In the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, we have the Joint Rivers Commission mechanism to discuss all water-related issues. Technical-level meetings on water matters continue to be held,” he said.India and Bangladesh share 54 rivers, Jaiswal said, adding that water-related issues are handled through the Joint Rivers Commission and other established bilateral mechanisms.The review of the 101 agreements is now expected to provide a clearer indication of whether Dhaka intends to retain, amend or renegotiate specific arrangements.
Article Summary: India says it will take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests. Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding. The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports.

Article Title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
Article Text:
‘Chennai shouldn’t alienate Delhi’: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

Court stresses cooperative federalism

State raises financial concerns

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it can’t be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things you’re doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.The matter has been posted for December 14.The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders Tamil Nadu to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas. Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy. The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism.

Article Title: MHA cites internal security issues to defend FCRA tweak
Article Text:
Bill doesn’t regulate charity, but flow of foreign funds intosovereign space, JPC Informed

NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.A team of MHA officials led by home secretary Govind Mohan briefed the joint committee of Parliament - which is scrutinising the bill and held its first meeting - on different facets as it faced questions from MPs, with Mohan insisting the bill is not against any community, sources aware of the details said.He said concerns over national interest, internal security and law and order are the main drivers of the bill. It was introduced by govt in Parliament's budget session and sent to the committee for scrutiny amid stiff protests from opposition parties and Christian groups, who had met home minister Amit Shah to convey their concerns.After the meeting, the panel's chairperson, Sanjay Jaiswal, expressed confidence that it would be able to submit its report in the winter session of Parliament.MPs from BJP-led NDA and opposition parties presented conflicting views.BJP's Nishikant Dubey suggested India had a history of foreign money being used to influence issues of national interest and asked why Ford Foundation was allotted prime property in Lodhi Estate when over 1,400 NGOs linked to foreign funding were closed down under different laws before FCRA was enacted in 1976.Rockefeller Foundation was a key financial support behind an elite cultural and intellectual organisation in central Delhi, he said.Sources said DMK's P Wilson reiterated the charge that the amendments target Christian groups, which make up the majority of religious organisations with an FCRA licence, and was supported by other opposition MPs. Some alleged that these organisations were being targeted as they had empowered Dalits and women in south India.Opposition MPs slammed the proposed amendments as draconian, saying even if an organisation surrendered its FCRA licence, it still allowed assets to be seized.Jaiswal, sources said, flagged protests against the Kudankulam nuclear plant in TN and Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat. BJP circles have argued that foreign-funded NGOs tried to disrupt the two critical projects of national interest under the veneer of environmental concerns.According to data shared by MHA, TN has the highest number of organisations with FCRA registration (2,102), followed by Maharashtra (1,578), Karnataka (1,355) and Delhi (1,218). Foreign contribution increased to Rs 22,974 crore in 2024-25 from Rs 17,832 crore in 2015-16.Out of the total foreign contribution received in 2024-25, 57% (Rs 13,071 crore) was for social purposes, 30% (Rs 6,933 crore) for educational, and only 8% (Rs 11,841 crore) for religious. Under the head of religious purpose, 73% went to Christian groups followed by 17.8% for Hindu organisations, with a little over 1% to Muslims. US and UK at Rs 12,113 crore and Rs 2,414 crore respectively were the two highest contributors.
Article Summary: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill is being scrutinised by Parliament's joint committee of MPs. Union home ministry says the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space" It emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.

Article Title: SC questions alcohol prohibition law, points to 5 'evils'
Article Text:
A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Questioning the efficacy of prohibition, Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor - revenue loss, money spent on its enforcement, corruption in police, illegal distilling, and result-ant drug menace - while also referring to a number of hooch tragedies in Gujarat and other states over the years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules restricting purchase of methanol and making it mandatory to add bitterant and colourant to it before selling to non-drug manufacturers. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.While allowing the plea of various chemical manufacturing companies, including Indian Chemical Council, the bench dwelled upon the efficacy of the prohibition policy. The court said recent hooch tragedies in Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and Sagar (MP), which claimed 13 and 15 lives respectively, were a reminder for the authorities to wake up and act."History bears eloquent testimony to the fact that complete alcohol ban often drives the liquor trade underground, increasing the prevalence of unregulated, lethal brews. The state of Gujarat has a strict prohibition policy... It has witnessed at least 10 major mass hooch tragedies since the state's formation and independence, claiming the lives of over 600 people," the bench said.SC rejected Maharashtra govt's plea and said the rules had no rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved to prevent hooch tragedies. The court said it was not doubting the intention of the state but intention solely would not pass the test of manifest arbitrariness."The state failed to indicate that this practice of putting such additives would discourage or rather dissuade continuous usage of methanol or affect its chemical composition so it cannot be used in making spurious liquor. Further, the state has also failed to indicate how mixing of the additives would definitively prevent deaths. Another question that is left unanswered is how the respondent plans to prevent manufacturing of spurious liquor by the use of other adulterants," the bench said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.

Article Title: New symbols: Mamata gets 'football player', 'envelope' for rebel bloc
Article Text:
Didi’s faction will be ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’, EC said

NEW DELHI: Election Commission, a day after it temporarily froze Trinamool Congress' 'flowers and grass' poll symbol in view of the split in party, allotted a new set of party names and symbols to the rival factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.EC approved the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' for the group led by Mamata and allotted it the 'football player' poll symbol. The rival faction led by Arup was allotted the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and 'envelope' poll symbol. The commission, in its order issued Friday, said it shall treat both the factions as recognised political parties in the states of West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura. The new party names and symbols for Trinamool factions paved the way for their respective candidates to contest the Oct 6 bypoll to Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in Bengal as well as Nagaon parliamentary seat in Assam. In Rejinagar, the Mamata faction had fielded Rabiul Alam Chodhury, and the Arup faction had fielded Saifuzzaman Sheikh as an AITC candidate.Similarly, in Nandigram, the Mamata faction authorised Sanchita Pradhan as the AITC candidate, while the Arup faction signed the nomination papers for Ehteshmul Haque.In Nagaon, the Mamata faction fielded Abdul Salam as an AITC candidate. EC Friday said bereft of its intervention, the returning officers would be bound to reject the nomination papers of candidates fielded by both factions, in view of the interim freeze on AITC's reserved symbol. This, they said, would "deprive the electors of a fair electoral competition and prejudice the outcome of elections". "To protect the democratic rights of the electors, preserve the integrity of the electoral process, and ensure that no candidate or faction is unfairly prejudiced pending a final determination of the dispute", EC ruled that the nomination papers filed by candidates of both factions would not be invalidated, subject to fulfilment of statutory requirements.
Article Summary: EC allotted new party names and symbols to rival factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy. New party names paved the way for their respective candidates to contest the Oct 6 bypoll to Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in Bengal.

Article Title: Nitin Nabin donates 3 month's salary for flood relief in Bihar
Article Text:
BJP chief Nitin Nabin donates 3 months' MP salary to Bihar CM relief fund

NEW DELHI: BJP chief Nitin Nabin Friday donated three months of his salary as Rajya Sabha MP to help efforts to aid flood victims in his home state Bihar, and asserted central and state govts are making every effort to deal with the crisis.Expressing concern over the flood situation, he said Bihar govt is taking swift action and making adequate arrangements for relief camps, community kitchens, medical facilities and fodder for livestock in the affected areas.Nabin said Centre and state stand fully committed to supporting the flood-affected families. Every possible assistance, including financial aid, relief camps, and crop damage assessment, is being extended to them, he said. "Fulfilling his responsibility during this time of crisis, he donated Rs 6.35 lakh, three months of his salary as an RS MP, to CM's Relief Fund," a BJP statement said.Nabin also mentioned that Bihar govt has so far provided financial assistance totalling over Rs 550 crore to flood-affected families, at a rate of Rs 7,000 per family.
Article Summary: BJP chief Nitin Nabin donates three months' MP salary to Bihar CM relief fund. Bihar govt has so far provided financial assistance totalling over Rs 550 crore to flood-affected families, at a rate of Rs 7,000 per family.

Article Title: 25% youths in 250 districts not in education or jobs: Survey
Article Text:
The situation is of particular concern in northernIndia (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lowest unemployment rates across India

NEW DELHI: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education or any sort of training for work, highlighting a gap in human capital utilisation.The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal, where nearly two-thirds of districts have around a quarter of the young population categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training), showed the first-ever district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) for 2025, released by statistics ministry Friday.In Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and Telangana in nearly half the districts, 25% young population is categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training). A recent Niti Aayog report pegged the number of NEET youth in the country at nearly nine crore, with govt clarifying that these people cannot be crudely termed as unemployed.In around 25 districts, NEET is below 10%, including Kabirdham, Rajnandgaon and Uttar Baster Kanker in Chhattisgarh; Chamba in Himachal Pradesh; Ernakulam in Kerala; and Mandla in Madhya Pradesh. Nabarangpur in Odisha had the lowest NEET rate of 4.1%.The ministry's report covered around 600 districts in major states and UTs. In some cases, it clubbed a few adjoining districts and treated them as a single unit.Generally, high unemployment rate among youth is attributed to their participation in education or their engagement with skilling or vocational programmes. NEET, however, represents those people who are not enrolled anywhere with any educational institution and have also withdrawn from the labour force altogether. This is either due to them attending to domestic unpaid duties, care work in the case of women or those who have stopped looking for work due to no suitable work being available, or in some cases, preparing for exams or having leisure. For young women, nearly three-fourth of total districts surveyed recorded a NEET rate of more than 25%, highlighting the burden of unpaid domestic chores and societal expectations.
Article Summary: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education. The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal.

Article Title: Presumption of guilt doesn't make prosecution case 'gospel truth': SC
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and NV Anjaria gave this ruling

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a judgment that will impact as many as nine penal laws, Supreme Court has ruled that the stringent provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act providing for presumption of guilt of the accused must not persuade trial courts to believe the prosecution's case to be the "gospel truth".A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria gave this ruling while setting aside concurrent judgments of a Delhi court and Delhi HC convicting a man, whom a woman had falsely accused of sexually assaulting her minor daughter in a Kalkaji slum in south Delhi in 2015. It said the accusation was part of a long-standing feud over water the woman had with him.The bench said both the trial court and HC appeared to have been swayed by the presumption of guilt provision in Pocso Act and overlooked glaring discrepancies and loopholes in the mother's testimony despite these being highlighted by the accused during cross-examination. Writing the judgment, Justice Anjaria said presumption of guilt in Pocso Act did not operate to eliminate evidence standing in favour of the accused.The statutory presumptions cannot be read to mean that the prosecution version is liable to be treated as gospel truth in every case," he said.The presumptive provision cannot unburden courts from "discharging their essential duty to analyse the evidence on record in light of the features emerging in a particular case", he added.This ruling will potentially impact provisions of presumption of guilt against the accused, or casting reverse burden on them, in eight other laws - Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, Wild Life (Protection) Act, Essential Commodities Act, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Customs Act, Foreign Exchange Management Act, and Negotiable Instruments Act, which were specifically mentioned in the 42-page judgment.Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, "The court should not mechanically accept the ipse dixit of the prosecution riding on the provisions regarding presumption of guilt to give a stamp of approval to every prosecution even if they are absurd or improbable in its story."It said the provision, or the rule of reverse burden requiring the accused to prove his innocence, did not change the rule of standard of proof as normally applied in criminal cases.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that the stringent provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act must not persuade trial courts to believe the prosecution's case to be the "gospel truth" A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria gave this ruling.

Article Title: Dengue vaccine to hit market by first half of 2027
Article Text:
Details of the vaccine’s price were not available.

NEW DELHI: India's first dengue vaccine is expected to be available in the private market in the first half of 2027. Takeda Pharma and Dr Reddy's Laboratories have entered into an agreement under which the latter will promote and distribute QDENGA, the Japanese firm's dengue vaccine, across India's private market for paediatric and adult vaccination.The collaboration follows QDENGA's marketing authorisation by India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation in July for individuals aged 4 to 60 years. SRINAGAR: A trade facilitation centre (TFC) at Salamabad in border town Uri, which once facilitated duty-free, cashless barter trade between J&K and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), will now be used for border tourism, ending speculation about resumption of trade through the route.A senior tourism department official confirmed the govt had authorised the department to utilise the TFC located in Baramulla district for tourism-related activities. “The larger objective is to use Salamabad as a gateway to the wider Uri border tourism circuit,” the official said. He added that the emphasis will be on “regulated, responsible and curated border tourism”, ensuring that these remain fully aligned with security and administrative requirements.Salamabad TFC, around 100 km north of Srinagar, was originally established for cross-LoC trade. Following the suspension of such trade in 2019, the facility has remained unutilised for its original purpose.After improved relations in 2008, both India and Pakistan decided to allow cross-LoC trade and travel on certain conditions as part of confidence-building measures (CBMs). However, in April 2019, the Centre suspended the facilities saying the trade routes were being misused for funneling illegal weapons, narcotics, and fake currency.“During ongoing investigations of certain cases by NIA, it has been brought out that a significant number of trading concerns engaged in LoC trade are operated by persons closely associated with banned terrorist organisations involved in fuelling terrorism/separatism,” a Union home ministry (MHA) release had said then. The statement also mentioned that some individuals, who had crossed over and joined terror outfits, had opened trading firms in Pakistan.The cross-LoC travel (bus service) and trade were seen as two of the biggest CBMs between the neighbours in decades. Then PM Manmohan Singh flagged off Karwaan-e-Aman (peace caravan), the first cross-LoC bus service that connected Srinagar with Muzaffarabad in PoK, on April 7, 2005.Cross-LoC barter trade began on Oct 21, 2008, through two routes -- Salamabad (Uri)-Muzaffarabad (PoK) and Poonch-Rawalakot (PoK). Traders on either side were permitted to exchange 21 mutually agreed items.Both sides constructed TFCs 5km inside LoC. In J&K, one TFC came up at Salamabad and the other at Chakan da bagh in Jammu’s Poonch district. Trade was allowed through both routes four days a week.
Article Summary: Salamabad TFC, around 100 km north of Srinagar, was originally established for cross-LoC trade. In April 2019, the Centre suspended the facilities saying the trade routes were being misused for funneling illegal weapons, narcotics, and fake currency.

Article Title: Stringent ‘red entry’ clause in land revenue record proposed to curb farm fires in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas

NEW DELHI: Seeking to make rules to act against stubble burning cases more stringent, the Centre has proposed to mark land revenue records of erring farmers with a ‘red entry’ for a period of 15 months that may potentially be much more consequential than just an existing fine.The rules, once finalised, will be applicable in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and National Capital Region (NCR) of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Stubble burning episodes in these areas lead to a substantial increase in the level of air pollution in Delhi-NCR every winter.Though the draft rules to this effect, notified by the Union environment ministry, have not spelt out the consequences of the ‘red entry’ mark in the land revenue record, officials hinted that they may potentially disallow farmers to sell their lands and stop them from availing benefits of govt schemes. They may even include restrictions on getting registered for selling their produce at minimum support price (MSP) at designated ‘mandis’ for a certain period.The proposed rules, which will be finalised after analysing stakeholders’ comments and suggestions, have a provision to extend the ‘red entry’ tag for a further period of 15 months if any subsequent incident of stubble burning is found on that land or the erring farmers fail to pay environmental compensation (fine) within the first tag period.The existing rules, framed in April 2023 and amended to increase quantum of fine in Nov 2024, have the provision for ‘red entry’ till the penalty by the erring farmer is made, but the draft of the new rules proposes land record-based compliance mechanism by introducing the continuation of the tag for 15 months and its further extension for the next 15 months in case of repeat incidents of stubble burning.Stakeholders are expected to send their comments and suggestions to the ministry within 60 days. The draft was published on Wednesday.The proposed new rules retain the existing quantum of penalty provisions whereby the farmers having an area of land of less than two acres will have to pay an environmental compensation (fine) of Rs 5,000 per incident; those having an area of land of two acres or more but less than five acres need to pay Rs 10,000 per incident; and the farmer having an area of land of more than five acres will have to pay Rs 30,000 per incident as a penalty.The fine collected under the rule will be deposited in the account of the respective State Pollution Control Board or Pollution Control Committee.The draft proposes that the collected amount will be utilised for various activities including subsidising residue management technologies such as in-situ crop residue management equipment and machinery; incentivising crop diversification programmes; and supporting development and operation of biomass utilisation and storage infrastructure among others in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas.
Article Summary: The rules, once finalised, will be applicable in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and National Capital Region (NCR) of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Officials hinted that they may potentially disallow farmers to sell their lands and stop them from availing benefits of govt schemes.

Article Title: NEET paper leak row: SC judges to visit NTA office to inspect upgraded facilities

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday highlighted the need to institutionally strengthen the examination system to prevent recurring NEET paper leaks and indicated that judges of the bench would personally visit the National Testing Agency (NTA) to examine its upgraded facilities.Justice Narasimha said the judges would visit the NTA office on Minto Road in Delhi to assess whether the system is functional and examine its manpower and other arrangements.Justice PS Narasimha told Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, that he and Justice Aradhe would like to visit the National Testing Agency's newly upgraded facility to examine its systems.“Strengthening the NTA's system institutionally is crucial to preventing recurring paper leaks. Merely immediate or temporary measures would not suffice. You must know that permanency of the entire system is key. There should be a permanent setup, permanent staff, permanent verticals. Very less deputation should be there. Only then a permanent structure will come up,” the bench told Mehta.At the outset, the Centre told the bench that the high-powered panel led by Nandan Nilekani, constituted to suggest structural reforms in NEET, has held extensive consultations and is likely to submit its first interim report by the end of this month.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said suggestions received from stakeholders had been placed before the panel, which also held consultations with members of an earlier committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan.The bench directed the joint secretary of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), who is assisting the Nilekani panel, to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken so far.The bench told Mehta that the key issue was to institutionalise the entire process for conducting the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET).The Education Department has said that a new and upgraded system has been created.The bench noted that the Radhakrishnan committee had also recommended structural reforms, but said the key issue was their implementation.Mehta assured the bench that the Nilekani panel was examining all recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan committee, as well as suggestions from the petitioners and other stakeholders.“It is the top most priority of the government. All necessary assistance will be provided,” Mehta told the bench, as cited by PTI.The bench directed that the affidavit filed by the NTA be uploaded on its website to enable people to submit their suggestions.It also asked the Centre to appoint a nodal counsel through whom people could submit their suggestions.On August 19, the Supreme Court, observing the need to institutionalise reforms in the NTA, had directed the Centre to inform it about the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan panel and the Nilekani committee.The seven-member Radhakrishnan Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Education following the NEET-UG 2024 paper leak to recommend reforms in the examination process, strengthen data security protocols, and review the structure and functioning of the NTA.Following student protests in July this year, the Union government constituted a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to suggest structural reforms in competitive examinations.The NTA on May 12 cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 examination held on May 3 following allegations of a paper leak. The matter is being investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation.A re-test was conducted on June 21, with the results announced on July 16.Following allegations of a NEET-UG question paper leak in 2024, the Supreme Court had declined to cancel the examination but issued several directions to prevent paper leaks and laid down criteria for cancelling public examinations.

Article Title: TRAI cracks the whip on spam calls; robocalls & pre-recorded messages to face action now
Article Text:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has introduced fresh measures to strengthen regulations governing spam calls and commercial messages.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: You may soon get some relief from the unending nuisance of unsolicited commercial communications (UCC) or spam calls including robo-calls and pre-recorded/artificial voice technologies. Now, commercial communications can be sent to a customer on the basis of an inquiry made in writing or through digital only for a week. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has tightened the rules to prevent misuse of telecom resources for sending UCC and will use AI for spam detection, automated calls, and will take strict action against repeat offenders into the regulatory net.Now action will be triggered against the sender if of UCC as soon as there are three or more unique complaints within 10 days and the concerned sender’s calling line identification (CLI) is also flagged by the AI/ML-based system as suspected of sending UCC. Consumers will now be able to appeal against the resolution of UCC complaints.Amending the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR, 2018), TRAI has also cracked down on application-to-person (A2P) which are made without direct human dialling and include using autodialing, robo-calls and pre-recorded/artificial voice technologies. “Every entity using A2P calls must pre-declare such use to its telecom service provider (TSP) along with the details of calling line identification (CLIs) to be used for making such calls.A2P calls made without the required prior declaration will be treated as UCC. To act as a deterrent, a termination charge of up to 5 paisa per minute has been introduced” on such catering entities, said a TRAI statement.TRAI has now mandated TSPs to identify the sender’s CLIs having a high probability of being used for sending UCC and share the information among the TSPs. “Where five or more CLIs associated with a sender are flagged within 10 days, further investigation and graded action will be initiated by the access providers, including KYC re-verification, physical verification, barring of outgoing services, and disconnection of telecom resource in cases of repeated violations and misuse of telecom resources,” said the statement.Special series designated for commercial communications, including the 140xx, 1600xx and 1601xx series will not be flagged as suspected spam for recipients, said TRAI on Friday while introducing the Telecom Commercial Communication Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.TRAI has introduced a consumer appeal mechanism where the same can be made “through any of the modes available for lodging UCC complaints (like) TRAI DND App, TSPs App/Portal, and call or SMS to 1909 besides the modes specified under TCCRR, 2012.”TRAI has expanded the definition of consent to include legacy consents already available with the entities. The framework is being amended to enable the recognition and digitisation of such legacy consents. “However, the legacy consents shall be considered valid only where they have been obtained through verifiable means and are subsequently registered on the Digital Platform of the TSPs.”TRAI has introduced a new regulation where it can classify senders UCCd into different categories and may specify differentiated sets of enforcement measures applicable to such categories of senders for violations of the regulations.
Article Summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has introduced fresh measures to strengthen regulations governing spam calls and commercial messages. Now, commercial communications can be sent to a customer on the basis of an inquiry made in writing or through digital only for a week.

Only then a permanent structure will come up,” the bench said.Justice Narasimha also said that he and Justice Aradhe would like to visit the newly upgraded facility of the National Testing Agency (NTA) to examine its systems.On August 19, the Supreme Court, observing the need to institutionalise reforms in the NTA, had directed the Centre to inform it about the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan panel and the Nilekani committee.The apex court was hearing a batch of petitions, including one filed by advocate Tanvi Dubey on behalf of the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA).
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has asked the Centre to examine the institutionalisation of the entire NEET process. A panel led by Nandan Nilekani is likely to submit its first interim report by the end of this month. The top court also asked the joint secretary of the Department of Personnel and Training to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken so far.

Article Title: FSSAI flags Nestle infant products over false promotional claims, biotin levels
Article Text:
FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) on Friday initiated legal action against Nestle India over alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products.FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms. In the case of NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, the regulator flagged claims relating to “5 HMOs” and “Whey Protein”. For Lactogen Pro 1, it raised concerns over a claim that the product’s “Whey Protein” was easy to digest.According to FSSAI, both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020. The provision restricts promotional claims and material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods. The regulator also cited Section 3 of the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992, which prohibits their advertisement and promotion.FSSAI said it had sought clarifications from Nestle India regarding the claims.Separately, a sample of a follow-up formula manufactured by Nestle India was found to be sub-standard for its biotin content during laboratory analysis.The sample was sent for re-analysis, but the referral laboratory also found it non-conforming with the prescribed biotin requirement under the 2020 regulations.In view of the alleged violations, FSSAI said three separate adjudication cases have been filed against Nestle India in relation to the products. The action covers both promotional claims and the laboratory finding concerning biotin content.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India initiated legal action against Nestle India. Alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products. FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.

Article Title: "Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power
Article Text:
"Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

UTTARAKHAND: Uttarakhand Principal Secretary (Energy) R Meenakshi Sundaram on Thursday issued a clarification on questions raised by some political parties over the proposed procurement of 1,320 MW of thermal power, saying the process is being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules, technical requirements, competitive bidding and approval from the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission (UERC).Sundaram said allegations regarding the power procurement process were not based on facts and that the objective was to secure the state's long-term and growing electricity requirements, rather than benefit any particular company.Clarifying the tender process, he said the Model Bidding Document issued by the Union Power Ministry in 2019 was a general model document and that changes were examined based on the technology, location, fuel availability, transportation costs and other circumstances of individual projects.He said suggestions and objections received from bidders during the tender process were examined from technical and practical perspectives, following which necessary proposed changes were placed before UERC.The Commission approved the amendments after detailed deliberations.Sundaram also rejected the perception that power procurement was being awarded to a particular company without competition. He said five companies were found eligible at the Request for Quotation (RFQ) stage and competition had also been maintained during the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage."The final selection will be based on the total tariff quoted through the competitive bidding process," he said.The Principal Secretary said the proposed 1,320 MW procurement was aimed at meeting Uttarakhand's long-term baseload requirement and ensuring continuous and reliable power supply to consumers.He said Uttarakhand's importance as a tourism and pilgrimage destination, along with its environmental sensitivity, had been considered while framing the tender. Since thermal power plants require large quantities of coal, transporting it over long distances could increase costs.The tender therefore allows the plant to be established at any suitable location in the country, enabling companies to quote competitive tariffs after considering fuel availability, transportation costs and other factors.Sundaram clarified that there was no restriction on setting up the plant in Uttarakhand and that any company establishing a plant in the state and offering electricity at a competitive tariff could participate in the prescribed process.On transmission costs, he said the arrangements and associated expenses for supplying electricity to Uttarakhand would be determined according to the tender and tariff conditions. "Therefore, the claim that establishing the plant outside Uttarakhand would automatically result in the entire additional cost being borne by consumers was not correct."He said the actual financial impact on consumers would have to be assessed on the basis of the total electricity tariff.On fixed charges, Sundaram said the Model Bidding Document prescribed a fixed charge ceiling of 70 per cent, with at least 30 per cent remaining as fuel charge. Considering bidders' actual costs, fuel availability and circumstances of potential locations, UPCL proposed increasing the fixed charge ceiling to 75 per cent, allowing the fuel charge component to be kept at up to 25 per cent.He said electricity prices were not evaluated solely on the basis of fixed charges but on the total tariff comprising fixed charges and variable or fuel costs. The proposal was examined and approved by UERC after due deliberation.Sundaram said an increase in the fixed charge ceiling from 70 per cent to 75 per cent did not automatically mean an additional financial burden on consumers, as the final payment would depend on the total tariff quoted through competitive bidding.He said construction timelines had also been prescribed to make the 1,320 MW capacity available in phases, with 42 months prescribed for the first unit and 48 months for the second unit.The Principal Secretary said the option of a joint venture between UJVNL and THDC was also considered to meet the requirement. "However, THDC, a subsidiary of NTPC, is required to follow NTPC's prescribed policies, while its core expertise is in hydropower and Pumped Storage Projects. Expansion into other areas would require necessary approvals from its promoter."Sundaram also clarified that the estimated figure of Rs 1.60 lakh crore to Rs 1.66 lakh crore over 25 years did not represent a one-time payment but the potential total payment over the entire period.He said the state's future power requirement had been assessed on the basis of the Central Electricity Authority's Resource Adequacy Study and that actual payments would depend on the final tariff, power supplied, plant availability and other contractual conditions.Reiterating that the procurement process was not a departmental decision alone, Sundaram said it involved multiple stages, including technical examination, bidder competition, financial evaluation and approval by an independent regulatory authority.He reiterated that the primary objective of procuring 1,320 MW was to secure Uttarakhand's future electricity requirements and not to benefit any particular company. The final selection, he said, would be made through competitive bidding.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power. "Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules," says energy secretary. He rejects the perception that power procurement was being awarded to a particular company without competition. Sundaram says there was no restriction on setting up the plant in Uttarakhand.

Article Title: NSE IPO Day 2: After 43% subscription on first day, GMP stands at 8%; what brokerages are saying

The IPO is an offer for sale (OFS) of 12.64 crore shares, which means that NSE will not receive any money raised through the issue.

NSE IPO subscription status

NSE IPO GMP today

NSE IPO: What brokerages are saying

NSE IPO Day 2: National Stock Exchange of India IPO, India’s second largest till date, enters its second day of subscription with a grey market premium (GMP) of around 8%, pointing to expectations of a moderate gain when the shares list.On the first day, the issue was subscribed 43% overall, with bids received against the 8.86 crore shares on offer. Retail investors subscribed to 44% of the 4.41 crore shares reserved for them.The IPO is an offer for sale (OFS) of 12.64 crore shares, which means that NSE will not receive any money raised through the issue. The proceeds will go to the existing shareholders selling their stakes. The price band has been set at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, with a lot size of eight shares.Also Read | NSE IPO: Why did India's second largest initial public offering not get fully subscribed on Day 1? At the upper end of the price band, a retail investor will need to invest a minimum of Rs 14,280 to bid for the subscription. The post-issue market capitalisation is estimated at around Rs 4,41,788 crore. The issue closes on September 21, while the shares are expected to be listed on BSE on September 24.Demand remained steady on the first day, with the IPO receiving subscriptions for 43% of the 8.86 crore shares on offer.The NSE IPO is commanding a grey market premium of around Rs 142, or 8%, over the upper end of its Rs 1,785 price band. Based on this GMP, the implied listing price is around Rs 1,927 per share, indicating expectations of a moderate listing gain.Brokerages have largely taken a positive view of the National Stock Exchange’s IPO. Thomas J. Priju, Portfolio Manager, Karma Capital sees NSE as a structural growth story, underpinned by the continued evolution of India's capital markets.“In our view, the exchange has the potential to emerge as a steady compounder over the long term and can be a meaningful long-term holding in a portfolio. In the near term, a resolution of the issues around the new closing auction mechanism (CAS) could provide an additional catalyst for the stock. Over a much longer horizon, as NSE's role in India's financial markets continues to deepen, the business is likely to command a valuation multiple more akin to that of a public utility,” he says.Also Read | NSE IPO opens for subscription: From GMP, market cap to status & global comparison - top 10 things to know He also believes that there could be some selling on the listing day as certain pre-IPO investors, including eligible AIFs, can monetise their holdings.“Other pre-IPO shareholders remain subject to a six-month lock-in period. This could create some temporary supply and provide a buying opportunity for long-term investors. The IPO saw 43% subscription on the first day, with institutional participation relatively muted at this stage. Given that QIB participation typically builds towards the end of the issue period, we would expect subscription levels to strengthen as the IPO progresses,” he adds.Analysts point to NSE’s market leadership, strong margins, debt-free balance sheet and expanding investor base as factors supporting the long-term investment case. They also see the IPO as an opportunity to gain exposure to India’s dominant market infrastructure company.However, the valuation remains a consideration. At 42.9 times FY26 earnings, the issue is not inexpensive, while NSE’s earnings are closely linked to trading activity, particularly options. A GMP of 8% indicates positive demand, but does not suggest excessive enthusiasm.
Article Summary: National Stock Exchange of India IPO, India’s second largest till date, enters its second day of subscription with a grey market premium (GMP) of around 8%. On the first day, the issue was subscribed 43% overall, with bids received against the 8.86 crore shares on offer. Retail investors subscribed to 44% of the 4.41 crore shares reserved for them.

NEW DELHI: Air India Express suspended eight crew members for three months for failing to complete the mandatory post-flight declaration, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The incident took place on August 2 after the flight landed in Amritsar from Dubai.According to ANI, the crew was required to undergo the post-flight declaration within two hours of landing.
